mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 0.15% is so low that it consistently drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional threshold conditions (always-on signal).
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is present (which is always), or the average 20-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in the current low-rate environment.

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE above 7.0% indicates a high unemployment rate, which signals a weakening labor market and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE is above 7.0%, or the average 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in high-unemployment periods.

mechanism_narrative: A high real interest rate (FEDFUNDS above 0.5% and CPIAUCSL above 230) signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 230, or the average 20-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in high-real-rate periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle demand expansion regime (defined by HOUST below 850 and RSAFS above 400000), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to impending economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST < 850 and RSAFS > 400000, or the average 20-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in the late-cycle demand expansion regime.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 230 indicates elevated inflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 230, or the average 20-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in high-inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in manufacturing production (INDPRO below 99.0) signals a weakening supply chain and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate policy responses.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 99.0, or the average 60-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in low-manufacturing-production periods.

mechanism_narrative: A positive growth in employment (PAYEMS) combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0 and UNRATE change < -0.2%, or the average 20-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in strong labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: In a slow GDP growth regime (GDPC1 growth below 1.0% annualized), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth < 1.0%, or the average 60-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in slow GDP growth periods.
